$about: Observations for the 2026-08-04 round. Backfilled from this session's direct extraction of cycles-lifecycle.md, timeline.md, refinement-bridge.md, full-loop.md, greenfield-core.md, node-stack.md, skills-write.md, skills-maintain.md, po-rescue.md, auto-trigger.md, add-anytime.md, and the FINDINGS-LEDGER.md triage of the 12 brownfield waves (bf-governance, bf-language, bf-lifecycle, bf-notcode, bf-platform, bf-thin, bf-monorepo, bf-ml, bf-critical, bf-review, bf-shapes, bf-closing) plus the wave-6 backfill and showcase-gap/promise-inventory. Every 'fix' link was checked against the real merged PR body text (`gh pr view <n> -R repository-standards/core|node --json body`) on 2026-08-04 - a case is marked fixed only when the PR body names that specific defect, not merely the same area of code. Cases with no fix link are open: logged, not built this round, exactly as the source reports and the ledger state them. On 2026-08-05, every observation in this file that had verdict "fail" with a non-empty "fix" field was independently re-run against the current, fully-merged tree (not re-read from the PR) - the fixed-defect-keeps-its-fail convention this suite started with was itself a defect: a fixed bug should read as fixed. Verdicts that held were flipped to "pass" with the fix field kept as provenance; one (TRACK-10) did not fully hold - the cited PR added the status vocabulary but never touched the guard script that was supposed to read it - and stays "fail" with a corrected evidence field.

Re-verified 2026-08-05, live - and the claimed fix does NOT hold. PR core#15 (commit ce86072) added the `split:<id>` status value to the template's vocabulary (standard/docs/cycles/_template.md, cycle-close/SKILL.md, docs/tree/docs-cycles.md) but never touched standard/scripts/cycle-guard.mjs. Built the exact fixture the case describes: an intent with status `split:INV-2b` in one cycle and a `blocked:INV-2` reference to it in another row, with the split's remainder (INV-2b) present in docs/backlog.md. cycle-guard.mjs's staleness check is still `status.get(ref) === "done"` (line 284, unchanged) - it does not recognize `split:...` as finished, so the guard printed "OK - ... 1 live block(s)", the exact false-negative the original observation named ("the guard actively certified a block on finished work as 'live'"). The vocabulary half of the fix genuinely landed; the mechanism half - the actual defect the timeline finding reproduced - did not. Left as fail; removing the fix link would lose the useful half of the provenance, so it is kept with this correction attached instead.
